Now, I'd like you to go look up a guy named Ross Perot. He famously ran for President a few times, most notably in 1992. Perot voters skewed heavily conservative and libertarian, and while it's a fact that Perot voters did not waste their vote, in a strict two-party election they would have voted for Bush by an overwhelming margin. To celebrate reaching 10,000 subs on this subverse, I'm happy to introduce a new sub: Gator Lounge.

This sub will be a place for GamerGate supporters and neutrals to hang out, socialize, and discuss off-topic stuff in an effort to get to know each other better. Over on Reddit, I've seen popular subreddits create separate social subreddits for this sort of thing, and it's worked out nicely. Considering Kotaku in Action's popularity, I think we could see similar results.

Whether Gator Lounge succeeds or not depends largely (actually, entirely) on you guys. If Kotaku in Action exists only because we're all united in our quest for ethical practices in games journalism and nothing more, Gator Lounge has no reason to exist. But I like to think we all share common interests in geek culture, a sense of creativity, and a certain uniqueness. It’s for those reasons I think Gator Lounge could succeed.

Plus, I have the blessing of TheHat2 when I proposed this idea weeks ago.

So head on over and introduce yourself. Share what you’ve been working on. Make friends. I’ll see you there.
